title: Sperm Chromatin Structure Assay (SCSA®) for Fertility Assessment
protocol: Reconstitute fresh or frozen/thawed semen samples as needed.
Prepare TNE buffer according to the recipe.
Prepare acid-detergent solution according to the recipe.
Prepare Acridine Orange stock solution at 1.0 mg/ml.
Prepare AO staining buffer according to the recipe.
Mix AO staining buffer and AO stock solution to prepare working AO staining solution.
Prepare AO equilibration buffer according to the recipe.
Use FCM tubing cleanser as directed for cleaning.
Obtain purified water for reagent preparation.
Prepare sheath fluid according to the recipe.
Maintain a water bath at 37°C.
Set up the flow cytometer according to Support Protocol 2.
Transfer sufficient volume of fresh or flash-frozen/thawed semen into TNE buffer to attain an approximate sperm density of 1–2×10^6 sperm/ml.
Add 400 μl acid detergent solution to the sperm suspension and mix on a lab vortex.
After 30 seconds, add 1.20 ml AO staining solution using an automatic bottle dispenser and mix again.
Place the sample tube into the flow cytometer.
Start acquisition of FCM data at 3 minutes after placing the sample tube into the flow cytometer.
Check the sperm flow rate; if it exceeds 300 cells/sec, prepare a new sample at the appropriate dilution.
Do not dilute the previous sample with AO buffer to adjust concentration.
Prepare a fresh sample if needed.
Maintain constant settings for sample and sheath flow valves during SCSA measurement.
Collect 5000 or more FCM events.
Measure samples one at a time rather than in an automatic carousel.
Ensure each sample is independently measured twice for verification and statistical accuracy.
Avoid delays between preparation and measurement to prevent artifacts from oxidative stress and dye absorption.
Monitor the sample stream flow carefully to avoid contamination and batch ruin.
Measure each clinical sample following the initial measurement.
Prepare and measure the repeat sample immediately after the first measurement is completed.
Place the AO staining solution in the FCM after measuring the repeat sample.
Run the AO staining solution through the FCM until the next sample is ready to maintain fluidic system equilibration.
Flush the FCM fluidic system with tubing cleanser after the last sample has been measured.
Place the AO-stained semen sample in the flow cytometer.
Adjust the FCM green and red fluorescent gains so that the AO-green fluorescent main population is just short of halfway up the Y axis on a linear 1024 × 1024 (or equivalent) cytogram.
Set the AO-red fluorescence to about 1/5 of the total X axis.
Make a horizontal gate near the top of the cytogram to exclude diploid somatic epithelial cells and leukocytes.
Make a horizontal gate touching the top of the cigar-shaped main sperm population.
Make a straight or curved gate on the right side of the cigar-shaped normal sperm population.
Make a 45-degree angle gate that touches the bottom of the cigar-shaped main population to exclude apoptotic and dead sperm and other seminal debris.
Use the computer to calculate %DFI and %HDS sperm.
Abstain for 2–3 days prior to collection to obtain “fresh semen”.
If abstinence period exceeds one week before the 2-3 day window, ejaculate twice, such as on Wednesday and Friday, then collect a clinical sample on Monday.
Alternatively, ejaculate morning and night for one day and collect a clinical sample two days later.
Ejaculate by masturbation into a plastic clinical specimen container.
Wait approximately 20–30 minutes for liquefaction of the semen.
Measure the sperm immediately after liquefaction using the SCSA test.
Transfer about 0.25–0.35 ml semen into each of two or three 2.0-ml cryovials using the SCSA test kit enclosed plastic pipette.
Tightly cap the cryovials and immediately flash freeze in the LN2 tank.
Contact FedEx (or equivalent service) for pickup of the LN2 tank to be delivered to a laboratory that performs SCSA testing.
Ship frozen samples without dilution in buffer or any cryoprotectants.
Place semen samples into an insulated box or jacket pocket for local transport.
Place small chunks of dry ice on the bottom of a well-insulated commercial shipping container.
Place the sample box near the center of the shipping container.
Place more dry ice around the sample box in the shipping container.
Ensure optical alignment of FCM using standard fluorescent beads as directed by instructions for the FCM used.
Pass AO equilibration buffer through the FCM fluidic system for approximately 15 min to saturate tubing with AO molecules.
Adjust the green fluorescent gain so that the mean green (AO – Green-525 nm) fluorescence value is at 475/1024 ± 5 channels.
Adjust the red fluorescent gain so that the mean red (AO – Red-630 LP) fluorescence value is at 125/1024 ± 5 channels.
Process green and red fluorescent signals as peak (or height) rather than area signals.
Choose a semen sample demonstrating heterogeneous DNA integrity (e.g., ∼15% DFI) as the reference sample.
Dilute the chosen semen sample with cold (4°C) TNE buffer to achieve a working concentration of 1–2×10^6 cells/ml.
Prepare several hundred 300 μl aliquots of this dilution quickly and place them into 0.5-ml snap-cap vials.
Freeze the prepared aliquots at −70°C to −100°C in a freezer or, preferably, in an LN2 tank.
